summary: Show the operator the drafted intake answers and wait for their reply
instructions:
claude drafted these answers from the idea (brief/intake-draft.json):
  idea: A mock self-help manual for a padel convert who has made the sport his whole personality, teaching him to talk about anything else, at home and at work. The humour is off court: what his padel obsession does to everyone in his life.
  title: The Padel Addict's Guide to Talking About Anything Else
  buyer: A wife or girlfriend, colleague, friend or sibling of a padel addict, buying it as a birthday, Christmas or Father's Day gift or a Secret Santa.
  recipient: A padel-obsessed professional in his late twenties or early thirties who took up the sport recently and now talks about nothing else.
  recognition_trigger: Steering every conversation back to padel and saying it is 'the fastest-growing sport in the world'; the padel WhatsApp group pinging at 6am; planning family weekends around court bookings; trying to recruit his dad, his boss and the neighbours; wearing padel kit to a toddler's birthday party; the racket bag in the car boot next to the car seats; 'quick padel stat' in work stand-ups and pushing padel as the team social; a 'padel holiday' to Spain sold as a family trip; calling tennis 'basically padel without the walls'.
  humour_level: medium
  visual_feel: classic_editorial_caricature
  colour_direction: muted
  print_colour: black_and_white
  cover_style: big_lettering
  main_character: user_description
  main_character_details: Josh, 31, a management consultant, married to Lauren, two children under five (Mia, 4, and Alfie, 1). Fixed look: short beard, a smartwatch he never takes off, and a padel brand cap or quarter-zip whether he is at the office or a toddler's birthday party.
  length: 80
  must_include: none
  must_avoid: none

Could not tell from the idea: none

Show the operator this summary once, ask the unclear questions, and ask them to choose the production policy (autonomous, visual_checkpoint or checkpointed; visual_checkpoint is recommended). Never choose it for them. Nothing is complete until they reply. Then record their reply:

  bookfactory intake padel-addicts-guide --confirm --by <operator> --policy <their choice> [--set key=value ...]

--set carries their corrections and their answers to the unclear questions. A new draft may replace this one if the idea changes.
